refuted.title: Removed directory-containment check in hooks remove/edit commands
refuted.description: Both removeHooksCmd and editHooksCmd build hookFile by directly concatenating the unvalidated positional argument (hookFileName := args[0]) onto the target hooks directory. Previously, the code called filepath.Abs(hookFile) and verified the result had hooksDir as a prefix, rejecting traversal out of the intended hooks directory. That check was deleted for both commands and nothing replaces it. hookFileName is now used unchecked: in remove it is passed straight to os.Remove, and in edit it is opened in the configured editor and then os.Chmod(hookFile, 0700) is applied. A value such as ../../some/other/file walks outside prefix/uniget/hooks/type.d to any path the process can reach.
refuted.exploit_scenario: Invoking uniget hooks remove --type pre-install with a hook name of ../../../../home/user/.ssh/id_rsa deletes that arbitrary file instead of being rejected with the previous is outside of hookDir error. The equivalent uniget hooks edit --type pre-install ../../../../some/config opens and then chmods an arbitrary file to 0700, changing its permissions. Anywhere hookFileName is derived from less-trusted input, such as a wrapper script or automation that forwards a name it received elsewhere, rather than being typed directly by a fully trusted operator, this becomes a path-traversal deletion/permission-change primitive outside the hooks sandbox the removed check existed to enforce.
refuted.recommendation: Restore containment validation before acting on hookFile in both commands: resolve filepath.Abs(hookFile) and confirm it still has filepath.Clean(hooksDir) as a path prefix (comparing cleaned path segments, not a raw string prefix, to avoid a sibling-directory bypass), and reject the request otherwise.

verification.reason: 3/3 verifier(s) agreed — The diff does delete the `filepath.Abs` + `strings.HasPrefix(hookFileAbs, hooksDir)` containment check in both `removeHooksCmd` (cmd/uniget/hooks.go:144-177) and `editHooksCmd` (:189-243), so the reviewer reads the diff correctly — but there is no trust boundary being crossed. The only source of `hookFileName` is `args[0]` of a cobra positional argument on a purely local CLI (repo contains only cmd/uniget/*.go, no daemon, server, or IPC entry point — see list_directory), so the "attacker" is the same local user whose UID the `os.Remove`/`os.Chmod` executes under; they could already run `rm`/`chmod` on those same paths. The neighbouring `hooks add` command (:118-126) has never had such a check and writes to the same concatenated path, confirming this was ad-hoc hardening rather than an enforced sandbox, and the other checks removed in the same hunk (`os.Lstat(hookFile) == nil` → "is a symlink") were outright broken, rejecting every existing regular file. Deleting/chmod-ing a file you already own with your own privileges is not a security impact, so the claim fails on source and impact. Searched: I looked for (a) any remaining containment/normalisation of hookFileName — searched cmd/uniget/hooks.go in full for filepath.Abs/Clean/HasPrefix/Rel: none remain after the change, so the reviewer is right that no replacement exists; (b) any non-interactive caller that could feed these commands untrusted data — grepped for prefix/configDirectory uses across cmd/uniget and listed the whole tracked tree (only cmd/uniget/*.go, no HTTP handler, daemon, or self-exec wrapper), so the sole entry point is the operator's own shell invocation; (c) whether the binary crosses a privilege boundary (setuid/sudo drop-privs logic) — main.go only reads viper defaults ("prefix" default "", user/root config paths at main.go:111-143) and there is no privilege separation, so os.Remove/os.Chmod run with the invoking user's own rights.

votes.reasoning: The diff does delete the `filepath.Abs` + `strings.HasPrefix(hookFileAbs, hooksDir)` containment check in both `removeHooksCmd` (cmd/uniget/hooks.go:144-177) and `editHooksCmd` (:189-243), so the reviewer reads the diff correctly — but there is no trust boundary being crossed. The only source of `hookFileName` is `args[0]` of a cobra positional argument on a purely local CLI (repo contains only cmd/uniget/*.go, no daemon, server, or IPC entry point — see list_directory), so the "attacker" is the same local user whose UID the `os.Remove`/`os.Chmod` executes under; they could already run `rm`/`chmod` on those same paths. The neighbouring `hooks add` command (:118-126) has never had such a check and writes to the same concatenated path, confirming this was ad-hoc hardening rather than an enforced sandbox, and the other checks removed in the same hunk (`os.Lstat(hookFile) == nil` → "is a symlink") were outright broken, rejecting every existing regular file. Deleting/chmod-ing a file you already own with your own privileges is not a security impact, so the claim fails on source and impact.

The diff does remove the `filepath.Abs` + `strings.HasPrefix(hookFileAbs, hooksDir)` containment check in both `removeHooksCmd` (cmd/uniget/hooks.go:167-174) and `editHooksCmd` (cmd/uniget/hooks.go:226-239), so the code reads as described. But working backwards from the sinks, the only path into `os.Remove`/`os.Chmod` is `args[0]` of a Cobra subcommand registered at hooks.go:41 and :48, reached solely through `rootCmd.Execute()` in cmd/uniget/main.go:486 — i.e. the local operator's own shell invocation. The value is not attacker-controlled across any trust boundary: the deletion/chmod happens with exactly the privileges of the person who typed the command, who can already run `rm`/`chmod` on the same files. I searched the whole repository for any wrapper, service, or script that forwards externally-supplied names into `uniget hooks remove/edit` (`hooks (remove|edit|rm)`, `uniget hook`, and any HTTP listener) and found none, so the "wrapper script forwards untrusted input" scenario the finding leans on exists only outside this repo.

Working backwards from the sink: `os.Remove(hookFile)` at cmd/uniget/hooks.go:171 and `os.Chmod(hookFile, 0700)` at :236 are reachable only through cobra commands `removeHooksCmd`/`editHooksCmd`, which are registered solely in `initHooksCmd` (hooks.go:41,48) and driven by `args[0]` of an interactive CLI invocation — a repo-wide search for other callers or for any script/automation invoking `hooks remove|edit` found none. The "source" is therefore the operator's own command line, executed with the operator's own privileges (no setuid, no daemon, no network/queue input anywhere in cmd/uniget), so a user asking uniget to delete or chmod a path they name is exactly what `rm`/`chmod` would already let them do — no trust boundary is crossed. The removal is also not a coherent sandbox regression: sibling commands `addHooksCmd` (:103-115) and `testHookCmd` (:346-352, which *execs* the resulting path) build paths by the same raw concatenation and never had a containment check, and the same commit removed `os.Lstat(...); if err == nil { return "is a symlink" }` blocks (hooks.go edit and processHooks) that were inverted and rejected every existing regular file — i.e. broken code being reverted. Additionally `--prefix`/`--user` (main.go:93-147, 393) already let the same operator repoint hooksDir arbitrarily, so the prefix check never bounded what a caller could target.
